name: Dave Cowens
summary: Made All-Defensive 2nd Team in 1973 and 1975. A relentless, mobile undersized center who pressed opponents all over the floor, and a core piece of Boston's defense-first title team.

name: Bob Dandridge
summary: A rangy wing who was later All-Defensive 1st Team with Washington (1979). He had no defensive honors in Milwaukee, but was regarded as a solid two-way forward.

name: Tom Gola
summary: Praised for concentrating on defense, passing and rebounding next to the Warriors' scorers. Versatile and known for defense in that role.

name: Hal Greer
summary: Described as a 'diligent defender', but known mainly for scoring. Never made an All-Defensive team, though the honor only began in 1969.

name: Richie Guerin
summary: No specific defensive writeups found. A tough, physical guard known for scoring and playmaking. Rated average by default.

name: Connie Hawkins
summary: Sources center on his offensive flair; nothing specific on his defense was found. His long arms helped, but his reputation was offense-first.

name: Spencer Haywood
summary: Known for scoring and rebounding; his defense goes largely unmentioned. He was athletic, but there were no defensive honors.

name: Bailey Howell
summary: A scoring and rebounding forward. No defensive commentary was found.

name: Lou Hudson
summary: A pure scorer. Teammates Bridges and Caldwell, not Hudson, were the Hawks' All-Defensive picks. He drew some praise for his defense, but not as a calling card.

name: Eddie Johnson
summary: 'Fast Eddie' was All-Defensive 2nd Team in 1979 and 1980, a quick, pressuring guard on Hubie Brown's defensive Hawks.

name: Jerry Lucas
summary: An elite rebounder who used intelligence to set up the defense. He was not a noted individual stopper and lacked athleticism on that end.

name: Maurice Lucas
summary: 'The Enforcer' was All-Defensive 1st Team in 1978 and a physical anchor of Portland's 1977 title team.

name: Dan Majerle
summary: All-Defensive 2nd Team in 1991 and 1993, a tough, physical wing defender for Phoenix.

name: Danny Manning
summary: Skilled and versatile, averaging about 1.3 blocks. No defensive honors or praise found; his reputation was offensive.

name: Pete Maravich
summary: SI called him 'practically a statue on defense'. Pat Riley said every guard wanted to face his 'soft defense'. His lousy defense was an open secret, though NBA.com says it later became respectable.

name: George Mikan
summary: A dominant basket protector who 'played defense like a goalie'. Goaltending and lane-widening rules were adopted partly because of him.

name: Robert Parish
summary: Averaged 2.6 blocks in 1980-81. SI credited him and McHale with restoring Boston's shot blocking, and Fitch praised his hustle getting back on defense.

name: Jim Paxson
summary: A scoring shooting guard. No defensive commentary or honors were found.

name: Willis Reed
summary: A strong, physical center on the defense-first Knicks, with All-Defensive 1st Team in 1970 just after this window. SI calls his defense underrated.

name: Doc Rivers
summary: An active, ball-hawking guard (171 steals in 1987) on the Hawks, who allowed the fewest points that year. Later All-Defensive 2nd in 1990.

name: Jack Sikma
summary: All-Defensive 2nd Team in 1982. Described as a rebounding and blocking presence, and Wilkens called him integral to the No. 1 defense.

name: Latrell Sprewell
summary: All-Defensive 2nd Team in 1994, a long, energetic perimeter defender.

name: David Thompson
summary: An offensive star; the defensive credit on those Nuggets went to Bobby Jones. Thompson was not noted as a defender and is generally viewed as indifferent on that end.

name: Chet Walker
summary: His NBA profile cites 'tenacious defense' across his career, but late in his career on the Bulls, Van Lier and Sloan were the stoppers.

name: Lenny Wilkens
summary: SI (1969) noted his defensive skill had drawn attention. A smart, quick point guard.

name: James Worthy
summary: Coverage focuses on his scoring and Finals heroics; nothing on his individual defense was found. A solid team defender in the Lakers' system.

name: Dennis Rodman
summary: Defensive Player of the Year in 1990 and 1991 and All-Defensive 1st Team, an elite multi-position stopper.

name: Bob Cousy
summary: Famed for offense. Sources say he was not among the quickest, and nothing praises his defense.

name: Cliff Hagan
summary: A hook-shooting scoring forward. No defensive commentary was found.

name: Derek Harper
summary: All-Defensive 2nd Team and 3rd in DPOY voting in 1990, with 2.3 steals. A premier on-ball guard defender.
